title: Trace Consumer Contract Gateway for Third-Party Storage Onboarding
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Background: We are onboarding a handful of customers who want to archive or query traces in their third-party storage (S3/ClickHouse/BigQuery) via vendor-managed retention. Current export path assumes a single canonical OTLP envelope and downstream Tempo compatibility; customers bring emitters that vary in traceid formats, sampling tags, and span envelope fields. We need a lightweight gateway that validates consumer contracts (schema + required trace metadata), normalizes common differences, and provides safe feature flags for permissive vs strict modes.
technical_notes: Design: implement a Trace Consumer Contract Gateway (TCCG) sitting between the internal trace router and sink adapters. Responsibilities: 1) contract validation (required attributes: trace.trace_id, span.id, service.name, sampling.priority if present), 2) ID normalization (32/16/128-bit hex, canonicalize to 32), 3) sampling marker preservation (copy sampling tags into span.attributes and set trace-level marker header for downstream), 4) optional enrichment hooks for tenant metadata, 5) backpressure signaling to router via gRPC health/fail-open flag, and 6) lightweight schema negotiation API for onboarding automation.
tradeoffs: Run-time CPU/latency overhead ~1-3ms per span envelope on p95; to minimise impact we will: a) batch contract checks, b) run normalization in a hot path implemented in Rust for the gateway, c) allow customers to opt into permissive mode to skip strict validations. Strict mode is recommended for archival correctness but may add latency. We intentionally avoid full-fledged re-encoding for each sink to keep throughput high; instead we attach normalization metadata for sink adapters to use when needed.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway deploys behind trace-router and accepts OTLP/HTTP and legacy JSON envelopes
Onboarding API allows creation of a consumer contract and returns detailed validation errors
ID normalization is performed and normalized_trace_id appears in span.attributes
End-to-end test shows preserved sampling marker and successful write to test ClickHouse sink
Automated canary run shows p99 latency increase < 5ms for tenant with gateway enabled
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalization logic and schema validator. Integration tests using synthetic emitters (Zipkin JSON, legacy Jaeger thrift mimic, OTLP) that assert mapping to canonical schema. End-to-end pipeline test writing to staging ClickHouse and S3 archive buckets; run a synthetic load at 50rps and 500rps. Add contract regression suite to existing trace-exporter harness (see PRs).
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy TCCG to staging as sidecar behind trace-router; 2) Configure a single non-critical tenant in strict mode and run 72h canary; 3) If stable, enable permissive mode for additional tenants; 4) Offer onboarding API to customers and run validation checks on sample payloads; 5) Gradually move tenants to strict mode when they pass contract checks. Must include automatic fallback to router-only path if gateway signals unhealthy.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create Grafana dashboard 'trace-consumer-gateway' showing: validation_error_rate, normalized_trace_count, avg_processing_latency_ms, backpressure_events, unhealthy_signals. Alerts: validation_error_rate > 1% sustained 5m for critical tenants, gateway_unhealthy -> rollback policy. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/trace-onboard/trace-consumer-health
risks: 1) Additional CPU on ingress nodes could push autoscaler thresholds — mitigated by vertical autoscaler and config toggle. 2) Incorrect normalization causing downstream deduplication issues — mitigate via canary and synthetic replay tool. 3) Unexpected customer emitters with non-hex ids — log and fail gracefully with advisory message.
next_steps: 1) RFC review with Platform & Observability (scheduled 2026-02-18). 2) Spike: prototype normalizer in Rust (2d). 3) Implement validator + onboarding API (1 sprint). 4) Add integration tests and staging canary. 5) Security review and RBAC for onboarding API.
